steps.name: Victorian Officer
steps.text: Do we... Do we need to keep increasing our reload rate?

steps.name: Victorian Officer
steps.text: Are you seriously trying to eradicate every mobile plate in the city?

steps.name: Sarkaz Warrior
steps.text: Got a problem with the general's orders?

steps.name: Victorian Officer
steps.text: I... I'm just concerned that bombardment on this scale will have an effect on the walls...

steps.name: Victorian Officer
steps.text: Nothing like this has ever happened before. If Londinium wants to swap out plates inside the city, we'd simultaneously have to shift around the walls...

steps.name: Sarkaz Warrior
steps.text: Didn't ask.

steps.name: Sarkaz Warrior
steps.text: Are you going to obey, or are you going to die? Those are your only two options.

steps.name: Sarkaz Warrior
steps.text: What's the matter?

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: I think he still has a third option.

steps.name: Sarkaz Warrior
steps.text: You––! Urgh...

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: Can you still stand, Captain?

steps.name: Victorian Officer
steps.text: I... I'll be alright. Who are you?

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: An old battle buddy.

steps.name: Sarkaz Warrior
steps.text: Over here! Someone snuck in!

steps.name: Sarkaz Warrior
steps.text: This shield? Where the hell did Victorian soldiers come from––

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: It feels pretty nice to use a weapon I'm familiar with.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: Captain, can this model of cannon... take out the control system of the city defense artillery?

steps.name: Victorian Officer
steps.text: No... It's not possible...

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: I was expecting as much.

steps.name: Rescued Soldier
steps.text: Horn, we've mopped up the Sarkaz outside!

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: Make sure to thank Mr. Misery again on my behalf.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: Captain, is there any other way to deactivate the artillery?

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: No need for the long face. You've been praying that we'd come.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: After all, you didn't even cover up your old ID from the city defense forces.

steps.name: Victorian Officer
steps.text: This is just a blunder. The Sarkaz... won't kill me over something like this yet.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: But if you help us, you'll be put to death?

steps.name: Victorian Officer
steps.text: And my family too.

steps.name: Victorian Officer
steps.text: They'll get dragged in. The Sarkaz can kill them off at any time.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: I understand.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: Carle, put your sights on this traitor.

steps.name: Rescued Soldier
steps.text: Um, Lieutenant... Where am I supposed to aim...?

steps.name: Victorian Officer
steps.text: Here. At my heart.

steps.name: Victorian Officer
steps.text: If I die... Perhaps only then, the Sarkaz will forget about me, and stop haunting my family.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: If you've made up your mind, we'll work with you.

steps.name: Victorian Officer
steps.text: Alright. Thank you, Lieutenant.

steps.name: Victorian Officer
steps.text: If you want to turn off the cannons, there are only two ways.

steps.name: Victorian Officer
steps.text: One, is to have the Sarkaz general stop them himself... The other, is to completely destroy the control room.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: For the first method to work, we'll have to defeat Manfred.

steps.name: Victorian Officer
steps.text: That's right. As for the second option... We don't have enough firepower. And besides... Are you prepared to tear down a cornerstone of Londinium's walls with your own hands?

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: I know it's what we should do.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: What about you, Captain? Are you prepared?

steps.name: Victorian Officer
steps.text: I've been waiting for this moment... for a long time.

steps.name: Rescued Soldier
steps.text: Lieutenant, you missed.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: Bloody hell, I suppose my hand slipped.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: Help him down the lift. Whether he lives or dies... should be in his own hands.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: Too much has happened on these walls today. We don't need to add another traitor.

steps.name: Rescued Soldier
steps.text: What about us? Should we head up as well?

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: Let's go. We're going to pay Manfred another visit.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Woah, this lift is going up way too fast––

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: L-Let's not talk right now... or I might vomit all over the Doctor.

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: After all, we've been dragged several hundred meters via zipline...

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Everyone catch your bearings? Enemies are approaching!

steps.name: Sarkaz Warrior
steps.text: We've got more intruders here! Report to the general immediately!

options: We'll catch up to the runner.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Closure, we need to find some way of shutting down those cannons––

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: If that means we have to take out Manfred, we'd better make it quick.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: The longer we take, the more the remaining Self-Salvation Corps on the ground will be at risk.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: *cough* *cough*...... *cough* *cough* *cough*...
To think you'd get blasted like this by a boy who's barely seen a fight... What an embarrassment you are.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Even a tiny metal crab, when backed into a corner... will pinch your hand.
You'd better hope Manfred buys your story.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: You shouldn't be here. It's too risky.
So you'd rather lean against rubble gasping for breath than let me lend you a hand?

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: *wheeze*... If you wanted to hold me up... the other side would be better.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Thanks to her, I can't move this arm anymore.
You ran into her. What did you think?

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Well, she noticed 'Her Highness.'
Then, she...

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Didn't change at all.
You're positive? We all saw what she was like back then.
Even when she was chasing down those assassins, her body riddled with wounds, could she have imagined... that Her Majesty wasn't dead?

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: She's not the volatile, impulsive mercenary she used to be.
So, she's getting even crazier?

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Who can say?

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: The truth is in front of us. She snuck into Londinium by herself and didn't toss a single bomb for two weeks. Not even Manfred noticed her.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: The way she was before, she would've rushed straight into Westhaleg and buried a hundred landmines under Theresis's throne before getting herself killed by Confessarii.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: I can reasonably assume she's formed some wiser plans with those folks from Babel... Or rather, Rhodes Island.
You almost traded your life away just to make sure of that? Aren't you playing it a bit too fast-and-loose?

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Manfred's underlings always have eyes on me. This was the only safe way we could meet.
Too bad for Schwab...

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: He made his peace the moment he sided with W.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Or should I say... We've all made our peace.
I sure hope so.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Who's there?
I smell... Confessarius!

steps.name: Confessarius Guard
steps.text: I told Manfred you can't be trusted.

steps.name: Confessarius Guard
steps.text: Hoederer, did you really think you could hide your clever little gestures from our eyes?

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: This is all a misunderstanding.

steps.name: Confessarius Guard
steps.text: Oh? Unfortunately for you, you won't have another chance to twist words around in front of the leader and the Regent.

steps.name: Confessarius Guard
steps.text: You don't need to pretend to bow your head anymore. Pick up your sword and revel in your last battle, mercenary.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: If that... is an order, then...

steps.name: Confessarius Guard
steps.text: You are powerless.

steps.name: Confessarius Guard
steps.text: You can't hope to protect your companions.

steps.name: Confessarius Guard
steps.text: Not a single shadow here... can escape my eyes.
Hoederer...

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Run!
No, you're not giving the orders here. It cost us a lot to come this far––

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Even more reason why we can't both die here!

steps.name: Confessarius Guard
steps.text: Worry not. I'll execute both of you here, together.

steps.name: Confessarius Guard
steps.text: You may take a moment to decide who goes first––

steps.name: Confessarius Guard
steps.text: Nngh?!

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: He went down... without a struggle?

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: You... It's you.

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: He got too cocky.

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: No one can claim to master all shadows. Infinite possibilities lie where the eyes cannot perceive.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: *cough*... *cough* *cough* *cough*...

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: Hurry, get out of here. If you want to live, return to the sunlight.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: What about you?

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: I still have other things to do.

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: I'll have you know... Confessarii underlings aren't the only ones here.

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: What's that sound?

steps.name: Self-Salvation Corps Soldier
steps.text: Commander, the metal structure behind us just fell––

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: That's not all...

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: He's here.

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: You feel it too?

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: Vina, I didn't hear anything except the sound of shelling.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: The sound of his heartbeat disappeared.

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Run!!!

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: We've lost contact with the 12th––

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: They've all been sacrificed.

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: Yes...

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: Their voices completely vanished.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: These... pitch-black pipes should amplify any and all sounds.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Breathing or footsteps, the clacking of a metal crab crawling through the pipe, or the rumble of machinery––

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: These pipes will record the vibrations of any signs of life.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: And in an instant... all of those voices were devoured.

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: You mean to say, this darkness behind us––

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Is all the life it has devoured.

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: Just like what happened at that banquet three months ago.

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: Engineering team, close the first safety lock!

steps.name: Self-Salvation Corps Soldier
steps.text: Yes, Commander!

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: Miss Siege, you've... got sharp senses.

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: Are you familiar with Londinium's underground structure?

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: I remember Feist saying... you're from around these parts?

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: I've... only been here once.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: But I've heard a lot of stories about these pipes.

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: A hundred years ago, a terrible fire ripped through the heart of Londinium. Only the royal family and a few nobles managed to escape the flames.

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: After that, a legend began to circulate that a magic circle was hidden beneath the palace that could allow the royal family to escape any disaster.

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: When I first heard that story, I couldn't help but wonder... would our royal family also use these very same pipes for their escape?

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Hmm... The story I heard was very similar to your version.

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: The workers who built Londinium, the posh aristocrats and nobles, and the royal family itself–– are all forced to take the same route during times of crises.

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: That already is a story that writes itself.

steps.name: Self-Salvation Corps Soldier
steps.text: Commander, the safety lock is starting to give!

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: This door cannot hold him back.

steps.name: Self-Salvation Corps Soldier
steps.text: Are you serious? This door's thickness can withstand seven or eight salvos from an armored vehicle!

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Retreat! Fall back!
With a sharp, earsplitting noise, a fissure appears in the middle of the metal door.

Under the tearing and folding of the tremendous force behind the door, the thick metal sheet seems thinner than paper. The fissure continues to grow, the dark void behind it like a monstrous, abyssal maw.

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: Close the second safety lock!

steps.name: Self-Salvation Corps Soldier
steps.text: Understoo–– Arrrgh!!
The door slams shut with a heavy thud, but the person sealing the door suddenly slips. Before he has a chance to scream, something invisible drags him into the shadows behind the door.
A smudge of blood seeps through the door's crack.
But not even the pool of blood is allowed to escape. In an instant, the shadows lurch through the door and instantly devour half the passageway.
Another massive roar rings out, though it is unclear whether it came from overhead or behind.
The pipe shudders, and the shadow's edge blurs like a predator's mouthparts, extending to latch onto its prey's ankle.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: I... I've also heard of another story.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: During a battle two hundred years ago, the Victorian Army joined forces with two other nations to lay siege to a city called Kazdel.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: One night, an entire army of heavily-armed troops disappeared in the valley where they were stationed.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: The count who had dispatched the army sent men to investigate their whereabouts, but only saw the crimson of the setting sun reflected against the mountain walls.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: And as everyone remembered, that day... the sun had not come out at all.

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: The third safety lock––

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Is this... the last one?
Clovisia doesn't answer her.
Just like her answer... Devoured by the monster flooding through the pipes.
